items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret from unworthy people?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains lowest men
items.inference: This teaching should be carefully hidden from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom and after what testing may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being identified
The chapter is the fifth
items.inference: The fifth chapter of the text emerged from Candradvīpa concludes here.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace has the speaker come to know the determination of Kaula?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
The object known is the Kaula determination
items.inference: The speaker knows the Kaula determination through the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What identity and essential nature are being asked about regarding the soul?
premises: The soul is said to be declared
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul's place of dissolution is questioned
A complete explanation is requested
The request is directed to the teacher
items.inference: The speaker asks where the soul dissolves and requests a full account of it.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme and unconditioned qualities define the soul's highest nature?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme
It is described as partless and eternal
It is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The soul's highest nature is supreme, partless, eternal, and untainted.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That supreme soul is identified as haṃsa
It is also called the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul who is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated within living beings?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
This air is described as situated
Its location is in all beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the given form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The subject is considered at the moment of leaving the body
At that moment a designation is applied
The designation is supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and perceived according to traditional lineage?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes down through tradition
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: This teaching is heard in the ear as it has come down through traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the traditional lineage.

items.question: What effect is attributed to merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing itself is presented as sufficient means
The fair-faced goddess is addressed
items.inference: Even the mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as efficacious.
uncertainties: The main clause continues in the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner is described as one who practices
The goal is a state free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The exact sense of kāṣāyaṃ in this context is uncertain.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What liberation and companionship result from the prescribed practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
Association with yogis is mentioned
Union with them is attained
items.inference: The practitioner becomes free from all diseases and attains union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching about the soul's practice has now been communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: A teaching has been told
The content is the practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the addressed recipient
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved recipient should this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one endowed with all states and of resolved mind.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a resolved mind.

items.question: Why must the Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
Its origin is from the yoginīs
It is explicitly declared not to be given
items.inference: The Kaula essence, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given out.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of sambhavam is slightly ambiguous in isolation.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is struck away?
premises: The speaker refers to her body today
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The body is now declared pure
items.inference: Today the speaker's body, once struck by ignorance, is declared pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish now
The wish is to hear something
The topic is the auspicious deception of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious means of deceiving time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious way to overcome time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can be destroyed without doubt?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: The speaker assures without doubt that death can be destroyed.
items.plain_english: I will tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: What paradoxical condition affects even the wise at the tip of nectar?
premises: The location is the tip of nectar
The essence of juice is involved
Even the wise one is burning
items.inference: Even a wise person can experience burning at the tip of nectar by its essence.
uncertainties: The imagery is compressed and may be technical.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one burns at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic action at the root of tongue and palate is prescribed for drinking the breath?
premises: A position is set at the root of tongue and palate
The breath is to be taken in
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: One should place awareness at the root of tongue and palate and slowly drink the breath.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink the breath.

items.question: What result follows when this practice is maintained for one year?
premises: The practice is performed for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are affected
items.inference: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to poison is claimed even after bites from great serpents?
premises: Poison is the potential threat
The body may be bitten by great serpents
Poison does not enter the body
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the practitioner's body.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
